comparator.name: Medical Informatics (Medische Informatiekunde)
comparator.academicYear: Current published UvA bachelor curriculum for a Fall 2026 entrant, checked 2026-09-27
comparator.sourceNotes: The official curriculum supplies an exact 60+60+60=180 EC pathway. Years 1 and 2 integrate healthcare, clinical reasoning, software, mathematics, epidemiology, information exchange, entrepreneurship and management. Year 3 has 18 EC genuine free choice, 18 EC taught AI and medical images/signals, and a 24-EC bachelor internship and thesis. No elective content is invented.
components: Genuine open choice; no specific elective content is invented.

core: Health information systems, clinical information modelling and interoperable patient-data management
Programming, software engineering and user-centred applications for healthcare
Medical foundations, clinical reasoning, healthcare work and patient safety
Statistics, epidemiology, health-data analysis, AI and scientific research
adjacent: Digital health, remote monitoring and responsible healthcare innovation
Healthcare organisations, processes, entrepreneurship and strategic information management
questions: How can health data and information systems support safe clinical decisions and coordinated care?
How should useful, usable and responsible software be designed for patients and healthcare professionals?
How can statistics, AI and process analysis improve healthcare while respecting clinical and organisational realities?

alternatives.label: Health information systems, data & care processes
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum integrates programming, information systems and data analysis with healthcare, organisational processes and responsible digital change.
alternatives.concept: A broad medical-informatics response combining software, databases, data science and AI with healthcare context, user-centred systems, organisational change, research methods and responsible information governance.
progression: Programming, data, research and organisational foundations precede data science, algorithms, AI, leadership, market research and digital transformation. All formal prerequisites occur in earlier semesters, planned offerings are respected and six level-3 courses provide advanced work.

alternatives.label: Biomedical data, clinical research & health AI
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum concentrates on human biology, disease, clinical research, statistics, biomedical data and computational approaches to health questions.
alternatives.concept: Develops medical data analysis and clinical decision support through biology, biomedicine, statistics, data science, mathematics and cognition, while retaining computing foundations and explicit research preparation.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, fifteen courses replace organisational, communication and software-systems breadth with life science, biomedicine, mathematics and quantitative disease modelling. The result is a materially distinct biomedical-data pathway.
progression: Biology, biomedicine, programming, data and research foundations precede molecular disease study, statistics, mathematics, data science and advanced quantitative biomedical work. Formal prerequisites and planned offerings are respected; six courses are level 3.

alternatives.label: Digital health, behaviour & healthcare innovation
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum emphasises how people and organisations adopt digital health systems, supported by psychology, sociology, communication, entrepreneurship and data skills.
alternatives.concept: Develops e-health, user-centred clinical technology and healthcare process improvement through computing and data foundations combined with psychology, cognition, sociology, communication, entrepreneurship and organisational leadership.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, eight courses shift emphasis from computing and general information systems toward psychology, cognition, sociology and human-centred organisational change. Seventeen courses differ from the biomedical-data direction.
progression: Programming, data, research, psychology and sociology foundations precede cognition, organisational behaviour, entrepreneurship, leadership, market research and advanced behavioural work. All formal prerequisites and planned offerings are respected; six level-3 courses provide advanced depth.

candidates.label: Biomedical data, clinical research and health AI
Digital health, behaviour and healthcare innovation

blocks: Statistics & Experimental Methods provides empirical study of human behaviour and evidence, but not medical professional reasoning as such.
Introduction to Biomedical Sciences supplies the closest scheduled UCR foundation for health and disease context, while UCR does not reproduce UvA clinical information-science integration.
Global Public Health provides the closest scheduled UCR population-health foundation.
Introduction to Cognitive Science provides human cognition and interaction context relevant to e-health use, without substituting for digital-care practice.
Perception & Cognition provides the closest scheduled human-perception counterpart to medical images and signals, without clinical imaging equivalence.
Introduction to Programming supplies the closest scheduled UCR foundation for developing healthcare applications, without implying clinical software training.
Introduction to Data Science provides the closest scheduled quantitative and logical foundation.
Databases & Web Technology supplies the closest scheduled technical basis for structured information exchange.
Introduction to Computer Science provides the closest scheduled software-development foundation, though not UvA medical software engineering.
Data Analysis & Visualization supplies the closest scheduled statistical-analysis counterpart, but not a complete clinical epidemiology sequence.
Artificial Intelligence directly supplies advanced AI study, while the health application context must come from the surrounding curriculum.
Machine Learning includes advanced independent analytical work closest to the data-research side of the stage and thesis, but does not reproduce a 24-EC clinical placement and thesis.
Research Methods & Statistics supplies research and evaluation foundations for a learning care system.
Introduction to Entrepreneurship is the closest scheduled UCR counterpart to entrepreneurship in healthcare, while remaining sector-general.
Operations Management supplies organisational and process context relevant to strategic information management.
The 18-EC UvA space is genuinely open choice, so no fixed UCR course is asserted as its counterpart.

selection.assessment: Three feasible and materially distinct curricula are included: a broad health-information-systems closest match, a biomedical-data and clinical-research direction, and a human-centred digital-health innovation direction. They cover the strongest evidence-grounded directions at the three-alternative maximum.

notes.text: UvA Medical Informatics is a dedicated health-information-science degree embedded in clinical practice, with medical reasoning, healthcare interoperability, clinical software, medical images and signals, and a 24-EC internship and thesis. UCR can construct related interdisciplinary pathways from computing, data science, health, behaviour and organisations, but does not reproduce that integrated clinical-professional sequence. The comparison indicates academic direction rather than one-to-one clinical preparation.
